language.script_notes: Dutch in the north, French in the south, German along the eastern edge, and both Dutch and French in the capital. Street and town signs often carry a regional crest that shows which language area you are in, and dual-language signage is common.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White post with a yellow rectangular reflector; some carry white or black reflectors.
road_furniture.line_paint: All-white markings: white centre lines and white edge lines.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility poles are common: square concrete poles with small holes running up them, similar to poles across the southern border. Town names are often printed on street signs; small square traffic signs with rounded corners are typical, and supplementary panels are usually blue.

architecture.roof_style: Dutch-style stepped gables in the north; darker roofs in the south.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick construction dominates houses and civic buildings.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Brownish-red brick with black or dark roofs.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Rectangular brick houses; the north looks like its northern neighbour while the south resembles Luxembourg and western Germany.

nature.terrain: Generally very flat, especially in the north and along the coast; the south-east rises into forested hills.

vehicles.plate_color: White with dark red characters and a blue EU strip carrying 'B'; the red text appears as a faint pink or red blur on Street View.
vehicles.plate_format: One digit, three letters, three digits (e.g. '1-ABC-123').

google_coverage.camera_generation: Gen 2, 3 and 4, captured from white camera cars.
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring; the red plate text turns into a pinkish smear.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same language in the north, flat land, brick houses
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Plates are red-on-white here versus yellow; utility poles are common here but rare across the northern border; signs show municipal crests.

confusion_set.shared_traits: French language in the south, similar-style utility poles
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The white post with a yellow rectangle reflector, the red-lettered plate with the pinkish blur, and small square rounded-corner signs are unlike the thick round white posts with a red band and 'AB-123-CD' plates over the border.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Darker roofs, hilly forested south-east, French and German signage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Red-lettered plates and regional crests on town signs.

confusion_set.shared_traits: German speakers along the eastern edge, similar brick and dark-roofed houses
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Red-lettered plates versus black-on-white plates with a district code; municipal crests on street signs.
